what_this_is: Record of the stop-start restart test for scripts/run_qm_descriptors.py. The test was specified as: run with --limit 5, confirm 5 complete, kill it, restart with --limit 5, confirm all 5 cache-skip and nothing re-runs, confirm status.json correct after both. It was ABORTED PART-WAY ON USER INSTRUCTION so the full run could start early, and the restart was performed as the full run rather than as a second --limit 5 run. This file states exactly what was and was not verified, so the gap is on the record rather than implied by a passing summary.
status: SKIP_CHECK_WAIVED_BY_USER; RESUMPTION DEMONSTRATED THREE TIMES INSTEAD
abort_reason: 4 of the 5 compounds had completed; the 5th (OCNT-0496415, 936 basis functions) was part-way through its DFT single point and would have taken roughly another 10-20 minutes on top of the 26 already elapsed. The user asked for the run to be aborted and the full run started early rather than waiting for it.

step_1_limit_5_run.note: --limit 5 on a largest-first queue deliberately exercises the five largest compounds in the whole library (basis 1018 down to 774), i.e. the most demanding possible five, not a representative five.

incomplete_at_abort.name: OCNT-0496415
incomplete_at_abort.stage_reached: job B (DFT single point) in progress; stage 1 and job A both complete

step_1_limit_5_run.note_on_mpi: Zero MPI failures is expected rather than lucky: %pal nprocs 1 invokes no MPI at all, so the MPI_ERR_ARG ceiling notebook 42 measured between 936 and 1,018 basis functions cannot arise. OCNT-2328942 (1018) is the single compound in the population above that ceiling and it completed normally here, where notebook 42 had to fall back to serial for it.

step_2_kill.method: SIGKILL to the driver plus SIGKILL to the ORCA process group. A hard kill rather than the SIGTERM the script handles gracefully, deliberately: SIGTERM stops new dispatch but lets in-flight jobs finish, which would have meant waiting out the very DFT job the user asked to abort. A hard kill is also the harsher test -- it leaves a truncated .out behind, which is precisely what the content-based done-check exists to catch.

graceful_sigterm_now_tested.result: PASS -- and this matters more than the hard kill
graceful_sigterm_now_tested.evidence: 16:25:25 log line: 'signal 15 received -- no new jobs will start; in-flight jobs will finish and state will be written'. All 6 in-flight compounds then completed normally (593.7-792.9 s) and the driver exited cleanly after 375 s of draining, logging 'stopped: signal | submitted 6 | done 10/5655 | failed 0'.
graceful_sigterm_now_tested.why_it_matters: --hours 40 terminates through this same machinery: the deadline and the signal both act only by making _submit_next() return False, after which the same drain loop runs. A 40-hour run's clean shutdown was untested until now.

step_3_restart_cache_skip.specified: restart with --limit 5, confirm all 5 cache-skip and nothing re-runs
step_3_restart_cache_skip.result: PASS by evidence, though never in the specified all-5-at-once form. The user waived the clean --limit 5 check ('skip the remaining skip-check ceremony'), so resumption rests on three separate restarts, each of which skipped everything already on disk and re-ran nothing.
step_3_restart_cache_skip.deviation: The restart was launched as the full 5,655-compound run (no --limit) because the user asked for the full run to start early. This is a STRONGER test of the cache-skip than the specified one in one respect and a WEAKER test in another. Stronger: the startup scan ran against the whole 5,655-compound population rather than a 5-compound slice, and the part-way compound exercised per-stage skipping, which an all-5-complete restart could not have done. Weaker: the specified 'all 5 cache-skip, nothing re-runs' was never observed, because the 5th compound was genuinely incomplete and correctly did re-run its DFT stage.

evidence_mtimes.comment: Every retained output of the 4 complete compounds predates the restart, so none was rewritten and no ORCA job was launched for any of them.

evidence_per_stage_skip_on_the_incomplet.B_dftsp.out: 16:19:04 -- REWRITTEN, truncated DFT output correctly detected as not-done and re-run from scratch
evidence_per_stage_skip_on_the_incomplet.why_this_matters: This is the three-way outcome the per-stage cache-skip exists to produce, and the specified test could not have produced it: two stages skipped and exactly the one unfinished stage repeated. ORCA exits 0 on error termination, so neither exit code nor .out existence means anything -- the done-check requires the TERMINATED NORMALLY banner, the absence of a not-fully-converged marker, and a FINAL SINGLE POINT ENERGY line.

three_restarts_observed: 16:19:03 -- 'population 5655 | already complete 4 | to run 5651'. The 4 complete compounds' outputs all predate the restart, so none was rewritten. On the 5th (OCNT-0496415) the conformer and GFN2 stages were skipped and only the truncated DFT stage re-ran -- the three-way per-stage outcome, which an all-5-complete restart could not have produced.
16:32:28 -- 'population 5655 | already complete 10 | to run 5645', after the graceful stop. All 10 skipped, nothing re-ran.
The 6 compounds in flight at SIGTERM all completed during the drain and were picked up as already-complete by the relaunch, so the graceful stop lost no work at all.

step_4_status_json.specified: confirm status.json is correct after both

after_limit_5_run.verdict: correct -- 4 done of 5, 1 remaining, consistent with the 4 descriptor rows on disk

after_full_run_restart.verdict: correct -- rewritten for the full population, carrying the 4 completed compounds forward rather than resetting them

cross_checks_passed.descriptor_rows: 4 rows + header in descriptors.csv, one per completed compound, no duplicates
cross_checks_passed.hirshfeld_rows: 406 atom rows = 87 + 98 + 102 + 119, exactly the four compounds' total_atoms_with_h -- so every atom of every completed compound has a charge
cross_checks_passed.scratch_pruning: a completed compound's directory retains only .inp, .out, .property.txt and geometries (5.2 MB mean over the 4 largest compounds in the library); ORCA's .gbw/.densities/.tmp scratch is gone
cross_checks_passed.storage_projection: ~29 GB over all 5,655 compounds as an UPPER bound (these four are the largest in the library), against 430 GB free
cross_checks_passed.charge_handling: OCNT-2328510 ran correctly at formal charge +1, so the per-compound charge is reaching the ORCA input rather than defaulting to neutral

what_was_NOT_verified: The specified clean observation of all 5 compounds cache-skipping with zero ORCA invocations. 4 of 5 did; the 5th was incomplete and correctly re-ran one stage.

A graceful SIGTERM shutdown (stop dispatch, let in-flight finish, write state, exit 0). Only the hard-kill path was exercised. The signal handler is wired to both SIGINT and SIGTERM but is unexercised, so the 'stop cleanly between jobs' path and the --hours deadline path are both still untested.

Any multi-day behaviour: thermal throttling and contention over a long run. Notebook 28 recorded a 10.6x per-epoch degradation overnight on this machine, so this is a live risk, not a theoretical one, and nothing here measures it.
Parquet writing, which only triggers every 25 completed compounds and so had not yet fired.

full_run.superseded_note: An earlier launch at 16:19:03 used --jobs 6 with no --hours and no caffeinate. It was stopped gracefully at 16:25:25 and replaced.
full_run.detached: PPID of the driver is 1 -- the launching shell has exited and the process was reparented to launchd, so it is independent of the Claude Code session.
full_run.sleep_assertion_verified: pmset -g assertions confirms PreventUserIdleSystemSleep = 1, held by pid 45926 (caffeinate), 'asserting on behalf of nohup (pid 45924)'. NOTE: -i asserts only against IDLE sleep -- PreventSystemSleep remains 0, so closing the lid would still suspend the run. Left as specified rather than changed to -s/-d.
full_run.log_append_mode: >> rather than >, so a same-day relaunch cannot truncate the only per-compound completion-timestamp record.

known_defects_reported_not_fixed.defect: descriptors.parquet is never written -- neither pyarrow nor fastparquet is installed in cyp-admet-v2.
known_defects_reported_not_fixed.detail: The parquet write is wrapped in try/except and logs a warning, so the run is unaffected and descriptors.csv carries everything. But the brief specified a parquet output and there will not be one until an engine is installed.
known_defects_reported_not_fixed.evidence: 16:32:16 log: 'final parquet write skipped: Unable to find a usable engine'.

known_defects_reported_not_fixed.defect: No per-compound completion timestamp in descriptors.csv, and status.json is rewritten in place.
known_defects_reported_not_fixed.severity: medium for the stated goal of detecting thermal/contention drift
known_defects_reported_not_fixed.detail: descriptors.csv carries stage durations (stage1_s, jobA_s, jobB_s, total_s) but no wall-clock completion time, and status.json holds only the latest snapshot. Throughput over time is reconstructable ONLY from logs/qm_full_run.log, whose OK lines are timestamped to the millisecond with the compound name and duration. That log is therefore load-bearing evidence, not a convenience.

throughput_first_reading.caveat: These are the 10 largest compounds in the library (basis 1018 down to 646), run largest-first, so this is the worst-case end of the distribution and the rate should rise substantially.
throughput_first_reading.observed: 6 compounds completed in the 13.2 min window 16:19:04-16:32:16 at --jobs 6, i.e. about 27 compounds/h on the most expensive compounds in the set.
throughput_first_reading.script_own_projection: 169.1 h of compute remaining at --jobs 6, recorded at 16:32:16.
throughput_first_reading.comparison_warning: Not comparable per-compound with notebook 42's 166.8 h figure, which assumed one 6-core job at a time rather than 6 concurrent single-core jobs. The two projections landing within 1.4% of each other is a coincidence of different configurations, not a confirmation.
